summary: Client singleton of mod.io mod-info requests in flight, used by ls::ugc::ModInfoCachedRequestSystem (macOS GatherRequests / SendRequests(HashSet<ModItemInfoID> const&, HashMap<ls::Guid, ModItemInfoID>&); Windows per-frame update bg3.exe+0x3BE8230): request Guid -> ls::ugc::ModItemInfoID. Two maps of the same shape (same Windows destructor as PendingModDependencyRequestSingleton). Live: idle, all zero.

fields.name: ModId
fields.evidence: ls::ugc::ModItemInfoID +0: macOS HashTable<ModItemInfoID>::Ensure (bg3_macos_x64+0x260BA40) hashes and compares this qword first; Windows default (bg3.exe+0x3BE8230) 0. Named by analogy with ModItemDependenciesInfoID's 64-bit item id.

fields.name: field_8
fields.evidence: Value of an optional 64-bit member: Ensure compares it (and mixes it into the hash) only when the flag at +0x10 is set on both sides; Windows default 0 (8-byte store).

fields.name: field_8HasValue
fields.evidence: The flag of the optional at +8 (Ensure: 'if flag == 0, value hashed as 0'; compared as bool); Windows default 0 (8-byte zero store at +0x10).

fields.name: field_18
fields.evidence: Compared as one byte by Ensure; Windows default byte 0 at +0x18.

fields.name: field_1C
fields.evidence: Compared and hashed as a 4-byte int by Ensure; Windows default 0xFFFFFFFF (-1) at +0x1C.

fields.name: Requests
fields.evidence: ls::HashMap<ls::Guid, ls::ugc::ModItemInfoID> (macOS SendRequests). Windows bg3.exe+0x3BE9CF0 (singleton through bg3.exe+0x3BE9010) removes answered request Guids from both maps, then inserts every new request (Guid hash '(lo ^ hi) % buckets', 32-byte value copied as four qwords through bg3.exe+0x3BEA130). Creator bg3.exe+0x3BEA800 zeroes two map patterns; destructor bg3.exe+0x682800 frees trivial values and the plain-key set.

fields.name: field_40
fields.evidence: Same map type at +0x40: bg3.exe+0x3BE9CF0 inserts only the requests of its second input list into it (and into +0x00 too). Role of that list not established.

open_questions: Meaning of ModItemInfoID's optional qword at +8, the byte at +0x18 and the int at +0x1C (default -1).
What distinguishes the requests that also go into the +0x40 map.
second_pass: Both maps settled on Windows from bg3.exe+0x3BE9CF0: Guid keys (Guid hash) and 32-byte ModItemInfoID values, the second map a subset of the first; the id's members come from the macOS hash/compare and the Windows defaults.
live_reason: only empty (all-zero) instances were seen: the member boundaries are untested
